title: Cast Iron Skirt Steak Sizzlers
seoTitle: Cast Iron Skirt Steak Sizzlers | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Steak fajita sizzlers—cast-iron scream, pepper char, not chicken fajita repeat
subtitle: Guajillo skirt steak strips, blistered poblanos, and sizzling iron for ten
description: Flank steak strips marinate in lime-cumin, sear on the griddle with peppers and onions, and serve on screaming-hot cast-iron sizzlers with tortillas.

steps.title: Marinate steak strips
steps.instruction: Toss flank strips with lime juice, cumin, chili powder, garlic, and salt. Marinate 2–4 hours refrigerated. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Use Mexican oregano as listed — measure each before heat goes on. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Prep peppers and onions
steps.instruction: Cut peppers and onions into uniform strips. Keep veg dry for griddle char. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat the flat-top griddle
steps.instruction: Preheat griddle to 450°F. Film with oil. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Sear steak batches
steps.instruction: Sear steak strips in single layers 2–3 minutes per side until charred and 130°F. Rest and hold at 170°F. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Char veg
steps.instruction: Griddle peppers and onions at 425°F until charred and tender, 8–10 minutes. Hold with steak at 170°F. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Heat sizzle platters
steps.instruction: Preheat cast-iron sizzlers on griddle or in oven to 400°F for service. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Sizzle at service
steps.instruction: Add oil to hot irons, pile steak and veg, serve immediately while sizzling. Warn crew—handles stay hot. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Tonight's line
steps.instruction: Serve with warm tortillas, cilantro, and lime. About 8 oz steak per firefighter. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

proTips: Single-layer searing only—crowded strips steam instead of char.
130°F pull for flank; carryover hits perfect medium-rare.
Hot sizzle platters need hot pads on the line every time.
tonightSpread: Cast iron steak fajita sizzlers with tortillas.
Guacamole and sour cream on the side.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Steak fajitas on cast iron deliver theater and aroma. Strips sear fast, hold at 170°F in pans, and sizzle again at service with a hot iron.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate steak 2–4 hours. Sear on griddle at 450°F in batches. Hold meat and veg at 170°F. Reheat cast irons to 400°F at service for sizzle.
